ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $CD$ is the altitude from $C$ to side $AB$, $BE$ bisects $\angle ABC$ and intersects $CD$ at point $E$, $BC=5$. If the area of $\triangle BCE$ is 5, what is the length of $ED$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct EF $\perp$ BC at F, \\
since CD is the altitude on side AB, and BE bisects $\angle$ABC, intersecting CD at point E, \\
thus $DE=EF$, \\
since $S_{\triangle BCE}=\frac{1}{2}\times BC\times EF=5$, \\
it follows that $\frac{1}{2}\times 5\times EF=5$, \\
hence, $EF=DE=\boxed{2}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, and C is at the lower right. Point D is located on side AB, and line segment DC connects from D to C; point E is located on line segment DC, and at the same time line segment BE connects from B to E, therefore E is the intersection point of BE and CD. The auxiliary point F is not drawn in the figure, and F needs to be additionally made on BC according to the problem meaning so that EF is perpendicular to BC. Reasoning: Construct F on BC according to the method, and EF ⟂ BC. The problem gives that CD is the altitude from C to AB, so CD ⟂ AB; also because E is on CD and D is on AB, ED ⟂ AB, and ED is the perpendicular distance from point E to side AB. The problem also gives that BE bisects ∠ABC, and E is on BE, so point E on the angle bisector has equal distances to the two sides BA and BC of the angle. Therefore the distance ED from point E to BA equals the distance EF from point E to BC, that is, ED = EF. Now use the area of triangle BCE to calculate EF: taking BC as the base, BC = 5, the corresponding height is EF, and the area is 5, so 5 = (1/2)·5·EF, solving gives EF = 2. Thus ED = EF = 2.
